attractions.name: Buddha Dordenma (Buddha View Point)
attractions.description: 169 feet bronze Buddha statue in Kuensel Phodrang National Park overlooking the Thimphu valley. One of the largest Buddha statues in the world, built to fulfil an 8th-century prophecy.

attractions.name: Simply Bhutan
attractions.description: Interactive 'living' museum giving a quick introduction to traditional Bhutanese life. Visitors are greeted with a shot of local arra (rice spirit) and guided through mocked-up village scenes.

attractions.name: Craft Bazar
attractions.description: Line of bamboo huts along the main street of Thimphu showcasing authentic Bhutan-made arts and crafts at reasonable prices.

attractions.name: Tashichhodzong
attractions.description: Largest fortress in Bhutan, on the northern edge of Thimphu on the western bank of the Thimphu River. Seat of Bhutan's government since 1968; houses the king's throne room and offices, the cabinet secretariat and the ministries of home affairs and finance.

attractions.name: Motithang Takin Preserve
attractions.description: Preserve for the takin, Bhutan's national animal. It began as a small zoo; the king decreed penning animals is against Buddhist practice, but the takin stayed and wandered the city streets, so the preserve was established under royal decree.

attractions.name: National Memorial Chorten
attractions.description: Most visible religious landmark in Bhutan, with golden spires and bells. Built in 1974 in memory of the third king, Jigme Dorji Wangchuck, in southern central Thimphu.

attractions.name: National Institute of Zorig Chusum (Art and Crafts Center)
attractions.description: Institute offering vocational training in traditional Bhutanese arts and crafts. Visitors can watch students training.
